The catch? Over 57% of the videos were uploaded from Nigeria! The AfD says it's nothing to do with them. Maybe. But that's exactly the point: synthetic reach can be bought by anyone to game algorithms. Users can no longer tell real support from manufactured hype. What lands on your screen has less and less to do with what we used to call \"social\" networks and more and more to do with machines steering your attention.\n\n🇨🇦 Global News Canada, on our other study: our analysts found 324 active ads on Meta openly pushing injectable peptides to Canadian users. These products are actually regulated as prescription drugs, illegal to sell without authorization. In the ads? Zero mention of prescriptions, Health Canada approval, or safety warnings. Meta's enforcement? Reactive at best. One ad comes down, the advertiser network behind it stays intact, and hundreds of new ones appear the next day. Whack-a-mole, indefinitely.\n\nTwo platforms, two countries, same story: the infrastructure for manipulation scales fast and the platforms seem unwilling to sacrifice profit for trust or safety.\nLinks to both interviews in the comments.
